"Let $\mathsf{Dias}$ and $\mathsf{Dend}=\mathsf{Dias}^!$ be the dual operads of associative dialgebras and dendriform algebras, respectively. For $n\leq 3$, multilinear identities of the Jordan diproduct in the free $\mathsf{Dias}$-algebra are consequences of right commutativity, $x(yz)-x(zy)\equiv 0$, and the pre-Jordan product in the free $\mathsf{Dend}$-algebra has no polynomial identities. Let $P_n$ be the $S_n$-module of multilinear right-commutative polynomials, with $Q_n\subseteq P_n$ the submodule of identities of the Jordan diproduct and $R_n\subseteq Q_n$ the submodule generated by identities in lower degrees. Let $P'_n$ be the $S_n$-module of multilinear nonassociative polynomials, with $Q'_n\subseteq P'_n$ the submodule of identities of the pre-Jordan product and $R'_n\subseteq Q'_n$ the submodule generated by identities in lower degrees. **Koszul-duality conjecture.** For every $n\geq 4$, there is an isomorphism of $S_n$-modules

$$
Q_n/R_n\cong Q'_n/R'_n.
$$

The conjecture explains the matching multiplicities of new identities for the Jordan diproduct and pre-Jordan product through the duality between associative dialgebras and dendriform algebras; the computed cases through degree $8$ support it, while the assertion in all degrees remains open."
